summary: Users can authenticate to Feature Store console but receive empty project role bindings after recent SCIM attribute rename
description:
Issue summary:
After a scoped Okta SCIM attribute rename rolled out last night (department -> team), newly-provisioned and recently-synced users can authenticate to the Feature Store web console but their project role bindings are missing. Users land on the console home page and see an empty project list (no projects visible) or 403 for project-level endpoints. The identity layer confirms an active session and SSO assertion, but the RBAC lookup returns no roles because the provisioning pipeline is writing the attribute to the wrong key in our identity store.

Observed start: 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC (coincides with SCIM sync job for Okta group rename).
Potential blast radius: All internal users whose Okta profiles were updated by the attribute rename; estimated ~120 users in prod-us-east currently affected.

Why this matters:
- Blocks engineers and data platform users from accessing Feature Store resources.
- Feature Store is used by CI jobs and infra tools; downstream pipelines are failing intermittently.

Expected behavior:
- SCIM sync should populate the identity namespace key that our RBAC engine queries (user.attributes.department) or RBAC should fallback to team attribute when department is absent.

Actual behavior:
- SCIM sync writes user.attributes.team but RBAC engine strictly reads user.attributes.department. No fallback. Resulting role lookup returns empty set.
impact: Approximately 120 internal users unable to see or access projects in Feature Store UI; several nightly model-retraining jobs failed due to permission checks. Customer-facing systems unaffected. Estimated business impact: medium-high for SRE/ML teams until roles are restored.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create or update a user in Okta and set attribute 'team' (post-rename).
2) Trigger SCIM sync (identity-sync job).
3) Log in to https://feature-store.console.redwood.ai via SSO.
4) Observe console home shows no projects or calls to /api/v1/projects return 403 or [] despite valid session.

Notes: Users whose Okta profiles still have 'department' (not yet renamed) are unaffected.
comments: 2026-03-12 04:05 - Maya Patel: Opened ticket after oncall reported multiple engineers couldn't access Feature Store. Attached initial logs and affected user list.
2026-03-12 05:10 - Samir Khan: Reproduced in staging by forcing SCIM mapping to write 'team' only. Confirmed RBAC resolver reads 'department' and has no fallback. Escalating to identity-sync owner.

2026-03-12 07:22 - Priya Desai (Identity Owner): The Okta change was intentional (attribute rename). We missed a compatibility mapping in identity-sync; rolling back is risky. Proposed short-term fix: identity-sync write duplicate attribute 'department' in addition to 'team' for 24h.
2026-03-12 07:45 - Samir Khan: Implemented hotfix branch to write 'department' alias alongside 'team' in provisioning. Deployed to canary in prod-us-east. Monitoring role resolution.
2026-03-12 08:15 - Maya Patel: Canary users report restored project visibility. Will await canary window before full rollout.
2026-03-13 09:00 - SRE Pager: Noted two CI jobs still failing intermittently; investigating token cache TTL interactions.
investigation_notes: Identity-sync: code path at identity-sync/src/okta_mapper.rs maps incoming Okta attributes into internal namespace. Recent mapping PR replaced 'department' with 'team' without adding backward compatibility.
RBAC service: role-resolver expects attribute key 'department' (legacy) as primary lookup. No secondary/fallback implemented. See rbac/src/lookup.rs:resolve_by_department().
Made a local repro in staging by modifying a user's profile to set only 'team' - role lookup failed immediately. When we add department to the identity record manually, roles resolve.
Okta product team confirms attribute rename was pushed as part of a tenant-wide profile harmonization change. They can push the attribute rename gradually but wanted to update SCIM sync ASAP.
Cache interactions: some users who previously had department populated retained cached role bindings for TTL (~15m) after rename; others lost access immediately post-sync.
Related config: identity-sync has a 'legacy_keys' option currently false; enabling it temporarily duplicates legacy attribute keys during provisioning.
resolution: Workaround deployed: identity-sync hotfix (branch hotfix/duplicate-dept-attr) writes both 'team' and 'department' into the identity record for downstream services. Deployed to prod-us-east canary 2026-03-12 07:50 UTC and full rollout 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC. RBAC service patch planned to add fallback logic and configurable key mappings in next sprint (PR referenced). Action items: 1) Merge and deploy RBAC fallback PR, 2) Add an integration test to identity-sync verifying legacy keys emission, 3) Coordinate with Okta team for future attribute renames and a runbook.
next_steps: Merge RBAC fallback PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/89 - add secondary lookup for 'team' when 'department' missing.
Add identity-sync integration test to prevent regressions (CI gate).
Schedule post-incident review with Identity and Platform teams and update SCIM runbook on Confluence.
Validate no remaining affected users after TTL expiry and cache invalidation (follow-up by SRE).
